Subject: Data retention & deletion SLAs — follow-up (SOC 2 / GDPR / backups)

Hi Jared — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

Summary of what we covered:
- SOC 2 status: Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II attestation (most recent report: Q2 2026).
- GDPR/HIPAA: We support customer-controlled encryption, data residency options (US/EU), and offer contractual terms for HIPAA covered workloads via BAA.
- Data retention / deletion: you asked about timelines for primary data deletion, backups, and log retention.

Action items we promised to follow up on: 
1) Share our SOC 2 statement and the vendor security questionnaire for your security team to complete (attached).
2) Clarify our standard deletion SLA language for primary customer data vs backups and logs; include proposed contract wording for your review.
3) Confirm the correct security contact at Amaya to send the questionnaire to.

Attachments: Redwood-SOC2-Statement-2026.pdf, vendor-security-questionnaire-amaya.xlsx, data-retention-sla-draft-2026.docx

Proposed default language (high level):
- Primary customer data: deleted/removed from live systems within 30 days of a deletion request or contract termination, subject to any legal hold.
- Backups & snapshots: backups are rotated and overwritten within 90 days; immutable snapshots are retained per backup policy but overwritten within 90 days where technically feasible.
- Logs & telemetry: operational logs are retained for 365 days by default; we can offer shorter retention windows on request.

Would you prefer we send the questionnaire to security@amayahealth.com or is there a specific person (name + title) we should loop in? Once we have that we can kick off the questionnaire and share the SOC 2 PDF.

Happy to hop on a short call next week if you want to go line-by-line on the SLA language.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Data retention & deletion SLAs — follow-up (SOC 2 / GDPR / backups)

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap and for the materials. A few clarifying questions from our security team: 

1) For primary customer data deletion: is "30 days" a hard SLA or a best-effort target? We need contractual language that says data will be deleted within X days — please confirm whether you can commit to 30 calendar days.
2) Backups & snapshots: our security policy requires that backups be overwritten no later than 180 days unless the vendor can provide a shorter defined window. Can you confirm whether Redwood can guarantee 90 days (as you suggested) or if there are edge cases where backups may persist longer?
3) Logs: we typically request 365 days for audit logs, but can accept a configurable retention. Can you provide the default retention and the mechanism to request shorter windows?

Also, who should our security team complete the attached questionnaire with? I see security@amayahealth.com is copied — is that the right inbox, or should we send to an individual point of contact at Redwood?

Can you also confirm whether Redwood's SOC 2 report is a public statement or a redacted attestation you share under NDA?

Thanks — Jared
Director, IT Security
Amaya Health

Subject: RE: Data retention & deletion SLAs — proposed language

Marissa / Rishi — drafted proposed responses to Jared's questions below. Happy for you to send these as-is or we can adjust based on legal input.

Answers / proposed SLA language (draft):
- Primary customer data deletion: "Redwood will delete Customer Data from active production systems within 30 calendar days of a deletion request or contract termination, subject to any applicable legal or regulatory holds. Deletion includes removal from active databases and metadata stores."
- Backups & snapshots: "Backups are rotated and overwritten within 90 days under normal operating procedures. In rare edge cases (e.g., disaster recovery snapshots stored for continuity), backups may persist for up to 180 days; Redwood will notify the Customer if such extended retention is required and provide justification."
- Logs & telemetry: "Operational and audit logs are retained for 365 days by default. Customers may request shorter retention windows via support; Redwood will implement requested shorter retention on a best-effort basis and document the change in the customer's account settings."
- SOC 2 report: "Redwood shares a redacted SOC 2 Type II attestation by request; full reports are available under NDA for customers and prospects undergoing security review."

Recommended next steps:
1) Send the vendor security questionnaire and the redacted SOC 2 PDF to security@amayahealth.com; request a single point of contact if they'd prefer someone specific.
2) Offer a short follow-up call with Neha (security/compliance) to walk through the questionnaire if they want a line-by-line review.
3) If Amaya requires hard contractual guarantees on backup retention (no >90 days clauses), escalate to Legal — that will be a contract negotiation item (possible exception to standard policy).

I'll prepare a concise one-page summary (Q&A) they can include in the security review packet.

Neha Kapoor
